findings.issue: The crop verification tables are not derived consistently from the supplied geometry. X positions mix document and viewport-local coordinates; many source-row values and CSS margins are incorrect. For CT03 at 320 the actual viewport is (20,3419,280,340), image is (-44,3361,408,451.34375): viewport-local offset is (-64,-58), source row at bottom is approximately 1171.05, and the conservative source-row-1180 margin is approximately +3.04 CSS px, not row 1183.2 with a +3.2 margin. At 360 CT03 reaches approximately row1124.19 with +19.76px margin, not row1184/+4px. CT02 at600 has local x=-14.117px, not an uncovered +5.9px offset; its bottom source row is approximately1084.05, not1091.9. CT02 at320 has approximately2.01px margin, not1.7px.
findings.impact: The declared numerical crop proof is false even though the inspected crops appear clean. A source row beyond a cutoff cannot be labeled a positive safety margin; mixed coordinate systems can conceal future actual edge/band defects.
findings.repro: Use localX=image.x-viewport.x; sourceBottom=(viewport.y+viewport.height-image.y)*sourceHeight/image.height; marginCSS=image.y+cutoff*image.height/sourceHeight-(viewport.y+viewport.height). Independently sampled original JPEG rows confirm CT02 transition around1100-1107 and CT03 around1184-1190.
findings.fix_direction: Regenerate the report tables programmatically from real geometry with explicit document/local coordinates, source units and signed CSS margins; preserve the conservative cutoffs and distinguish source pixels from rendered CSS pixels. Do not change currently clean crops merely to match the erroneous table.

findings.issue: The report labels several acceptance checks as executed that the tests do not establish. FAQ interaction directly focuses the second button, presses Enter/Space and clicks the first; the Tab/Shift+Tab loop at line93 is inside the Header dialog, not through FAQ controls. There is no FAQ forward/reverse traversal or explicit accessibility-tree exclusion check. Collapsed panels use native hidden only, not the claimed aria-hidden+hidden; native hidden is appropriate and does not need redundant ARIA. The image decode loop swallows decode failures and never asserts all image natural sizes or required request success. No reduced-motion assertion is present in the inspected tests.
findings.impact: The page's required keyboard/accessibility and asset checks are overclaimed, so the checklist cannot be used as proof that the specified acceptance coverage ran.
findings.repro: Read the actual FAQ test and chrome test; search for FAQ Tab/Shift+Tab traversal, accessibility-tree/hidden-text assertions, failed-required-request assertions and reduced-motion checks. Those checks are not present in the supplied execution scope.
findings.fix_direction: Complete focused FAQ keyboard and hidden-content verification and required-image checks; distinguish actual executed assertions from native-semantic/source inspection and not-applicable motion. Correct the report rather than adding unnecessary ARIA or manufacturing checks.
